newsitem.title: FRANCE: Morton Cie des Salins bid worth 1.5 bln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: Morton Cie des Salins bid worth 1.5 bln Ffr.

text.p: Morton International's agreement on Tuesday to take over Cie des Salins du Midi et des Salines de l'Est, Europe's largest saltmaker, values the company at 1.5 billion francs, French newspapers said on Thursday.
Morton will pay 614 francs per share or about 772 million francs for the 50.8 percent of Cie des Salins held by Cie de Suez unit Suez Industrie.

Morton will also buy stakes, on the same terms, held by l'Union d'Etudes et d'Investissement and the Rougie family for an immediate purchase of 67.6 percent of the company's capital and 66.5 percent of the voting rights.
The offer price represents a 40-percent premium over the 440-franc price at which Cie des Salins last traded.
The company's shares have been suspended since December 23 when Suez said it was in talks about a possible sale of the stake. Trading in Cie des Salins will resume on January 3.
Suez said the deal would produce a capital gain but did not give a figure.
In a statement on Tuesday Suez said Morton planned to make a public offer on the same terms to take over publicly-held shares of Cie des Salins once the deal with Suez was complete.
Suez said the deal was conditional on approval from the ministry of industry.
Suez said Morton planned to maintain Cie des Salins' French and European identity through its decentralised operations.
No one at Suez was available for comment on the deal on Thursday but it fits well with Suez's ongoing strategy to concentrate on infrastructure services and financial services.
Financial daily Les Echos quoted an official with Bankers Trust, which helped negotiate the sale, saying the deal made sense.
"It was the logical buyer. It had no presence in Europe," the paper quoted the official as saying.
